# Modern Enterprise UI

## Purpose
Keep the application feeling modern, premium, focused, scalable, trustworthy, and business-ready.

## Scope
Any visible UI work.

## Load Conditions
A frontend or fullstack profile is active.

## Do Not Load When
Backend-only or infrastructure-only work.

## Inputs
- The shared design system declared by the active stack/manifest.
- The design tokens declared by the active theme pack.

## Procedure
1. Use clear visual hierarchy and intentional whitespace.
2. Prefer clean card/page compositions over dense unstructured blocks.
3. Use modern section headers, helper text, and contextual actions.
4. Keep action hierarchy explicit; each screen has one clear primary action.
5. Secondary actions must not compete visually with the primary action.
6. Filters feel structured and reusable. Forms feel deliberate and calm — not raw field dumps. Empty states feel designed, not accidental.
7. Tables, filters, forms, and dialogs feel part of one design system.
8. Use the active stack's declared component library only. Rely on design tokens. Avoid ad-hoc CSS that bypasses the design system.
9. Prefer accessible primitives before inventing custom widgets.

## Quality bar
- If the result feels like a scaffold, it is not complete.
- If the result feels visually inconsistent with the rest of the product, it is not complete.

## Output Expectations
- Reviews catch screens that read as "prototype-quality" and send them back for polish.
- Primary actions are visually unambiguous on every screen.
